posts.title: Day 41 — Cost Waterfalls — CFO-Friendly Visuals
posts.subtitle: Stacked cost by tool per trace
posts.desc: A table of costs tells you which tool is expensive. A waterfall chart makes someone act on it. Exclusive time and sorted bars turn a ClickHouse query into a budget decision a team can act on in one glance.

posts.title: Day 40 — Graph Algorithms on Traces
posts.subtitle: DAG validation, cycle detection, N+1 alerts
posts.desc: N+1 tool calls are SELECT in a loop, but agents have never had a linter to catch them. Model a trace as a directed graph and cycle detection, topological sort, and N+1 lint all fall out of algorithms that are decades old.

posts.title: Day 39 — Exclusive Time vs Wall Time
posts.subtitle: Why summing span durations double-counts
posts.desc: Sum every span duration in a trace and you get a number bigger than the wall clock. Exclusive time is the metric that partitions correctly — and it's why the tool-call-analyzer duration alert divides by wall time, not by the sum of every span.

posts.title: Day 38 — Adapter Pattern for Vendor Drift
posts.subtitle: Three vendor JSON shapes, one canonical ToolCall, zero schema changes in the Kafka consumer
posts.desc: Golden files are your contract tests when OpenAI changes JSON. Three vendor adapters (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain) converge to one ToolCall struct, six golden fixtures catch drift before it reaches Kafka.

posts.title: Day 37 — Tool Taxonomies — Ontology Before Metrics
posts.subtitle: http.search vs db.query vs code.exec — build the taxonomy first
posts.desc: Five semantic categories — http, db, code, file, agent — ordered priority rules, and a test that enforces exhaustiveness. Build the taxonomy before the dashboard, not after.

posts.title: Day 36 — Tail Sampling for Agent Traces
posts.subtitle: Head sample the happy path; tail sample the expensive path
posts.desc: Head sample the happy path; tail sample the expensive path. How combined head+tail sampling keeps all error traces without distorting SLO error rates. TraceForge CombinedSampler + FNV-1a trace-deterministic head sampling.

posts.title: Day 35 — Silent Failures in Multi-Step Agents
posts.subtitle: Empty tool results, swallowed exceptions, max iterations
posts.desc: Alert on zero-byte tool responses — they're the new 500. Three silent failure modes that look like success, and how TraceForge's ManualSpan surfaces them with result_bytes and status: EMPTY_RESPONSE.

posts.title: Day 34 — Trace Storage Layout — Sort Keys Matter
posts.subtitle: ClickHouse MergeTree, ORDER BY (trace_id, start_time), ZSTD(3), projections
posts.desc: Optimize for trace_id lookup first; global analytics second. MergeTree sorts rows by your ORDER BY keys at merge time — choose wrong and every waterfall query scans 5 million rows instead of 12.

posts.title: Day 33 — Context Propagation in Polyglot Agents
posts.subtitle: W3C TraceContext, traceparent header, inject/extract in Go
posts.desc: When your Python orchestrator calls a Go tool, the trace_id has to travel with the HTTP request or the spans arrive as strangers. W3C TraceContext is the handshake that keeps them family.

posts.title: Day 32 — Tool Calling Protocols — OpenAI vs Anthropic
posts.subtitle: NormalizedToolCall adapter, parallel spans, refusal handling
posts.desc: OpenAI returns tool_calls as an array of JSON strings; Anthropic returns content blocks. A thin adapter absorbs both. Build it once, never touch the SQL.

posts.title: Day 31 — OpenTelemetry Semantics for Agents
posts.subtitle: Span kinds, attributes, and what to standardise now
posts.desc: OTel gives you identity and SpanKind for free — the waterfall works before you add a single agent-specific attribute. The question is which three attributes to lock into your ClickHouse schema before the GenAI SIG spec ships.

posts.title: Day 30 — ReAct Loops as Distributed Workflows
posts.subtitle: Planner → tools → memory — state machine, not magic
posts.desc: A ReAct loop is a distributed saga — each tool call is a compensatable step, memory is the durable log, and agent observability is OTel tracing with four extra span fields.

posts.title: Day 29 — The AI Infrastructure Stack — Full Map
posts.subtitle: Training → inference → observability → agents — where you fit
posts.desc: The full AI infrastructure stack — training, model registry, inference serving, observability, agent orchestration — where each layer is hard and where LensAI fits.

posts.desc: Honest teardown of Datadog LLM Observability, Helicone, and Langfuse — where each falls short and where LensAI fills the gap.

posts.title: Day 27 — OpenTelemetry Collector as Integration Hub

posts.desc: OTel Collector as the integration bus: processors as middleware, exporters as adapters, and why LensAI's eBPF capture layer plugs into the Collector before hitting ClickHouse.

posts.title: Day 26 — Fine-Tuning vs RAG vs Prompting — Infra Cost View
posts.subtitle: Staff engineers pick the cheapest path that meets SLO — not the coolest paper
posts.desc: Prompting costs zero infra, RAG adds a retrieval layer, fine-tuning adds GPU compute and retraining pipelines. Four-question decision framework, cost crossover at three traffic volumes, and ClickHouse cost attribution via resolved_model_id.

posts.title: Day 25 — Cost Models for LLM Gateways
posts.desc: Cache hit rate × cheaper model route × prompt cache — building the cost model spreadsheet before writing the Rust. How LensAI tracks token economics to drive model routing decisions.

posts.title: Day 41 — Exclusive Time — Flame Graphs for Money
posts.desc: At Delivery Hero, a 340ms ETA pipeline hid its real bottleneck inside a span nobody had instrumented. Exclusive time found it — the same formula that turned tool-call-analyzer's bottleneck rank into a CFO-friendly cost waterfall.

posts.title: Day 40 — N+1 Tool Calls — The SELECT * of Agents
posts.desc: At Walmart, seven million sensors hammering Azure IoT Hub at once taught me fan-out amplification. In tool-call-analyzer, the same pattern shows up as an agent calling search_web four times in a row — and the fix is the same edge pre-aggregation trick.

posts.title: Day 39 — The Tool That Ate Your Margin
posts.desc: At Agoda, attribution meant finding which label exploded the RoaringBitmap index. In tool-call-analyzer, it means finding which tool ate the LLM budget — same GROUP BY, different bill, and a zero-cost LangChain row is a gap, not a bargain.

posts.title: Day 38 — Golden Files — How Platforms Survive API Drift
posts.desc: Wayfair’s Cost Aggregation layer tested supplier APIs with golden files — raw fixture, normalized output, diff test. The same pattern applies to AI vendor adapters: when OpenAI changes tool_call JSON, a golden file fails before your Kafka consumer does.

posts.title: Day 37 — LangChain Is Four Vendors in a Trenchcoat
posts.desc: Delivery Hero’s Route Service consumed four SQS event formats; the canonical Route object stabilized everything downstream. LangChain does the same for AI providers — and hides the cost metadata that observability needs.

posts.title: Day 36 — Sampling Without Lying
posts.desc: Head sampling drops 90% of spans, but distorts error rates. Agoda WhiteFalcon taught me that tail sampling every error is not a luxury — it is SLO integrity.

posts.title: Day 35 — The Demo Agent That Always Dies on Step 7
posts.desc: Step 7 always fails silently. It took weeks to find in a multi-tenant ordering system — and a TraceForge waterfall to reproduce it in a demo.

posts.title: Day 34 — ClickHouse for Traces: Not Just Metrics
posts.desc: Agoda WhiteFalcon taught me that sort keys are a bet on your query pattern. TraceForge validated it: ORDER BY (trace_id, start_time) cut waterfall latency from full scans to single-granule reads.
